proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad
 D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.
\tag{10}
\]
By \texttt{lem:causal-identification}, consistency and event-date transport
give the observed-law equality
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \{\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus (11) is derived from the causal estimand and is not its definition.

We first analyze the total estimator in
\texttt{def:nearest-design-estimator}.  Conditional on \(z_0\), the exact
design, and the donor sample, let \(t_{s\ell}\) be its selected nearest
indices and define
\[
 U_{si}=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 -\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)
 -K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
   \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-m_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} makes (12)
conditionally mean zero.  Assumptions
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} and
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} make these variables independent over
\((s,i)\) after the displayed conditioning.  The fold weights are
nonnegative and sum to one; bounded wealth therefore gives
\(|U_{si}|\le4B\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
   \sum_s\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_iU_{si}
   \mathrel{\Big|}z_0,(X_{st}),(Z_j)\right)
 \le16B^2A.
\tag{13}
\]

Nearest-neighbor optimality and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_{0s}\|_2
 \le \rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_{0s}\|_2.
\tag{14}
\]
Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), subadditivity of \(x\mapsto x^\lambda\) and
Holder smoothness imply
\[
 |m_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-m_s(z_{0s})|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda
       +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive.  If \(m_\ell=|I_\ell|\), balanced
splitting gives \(m_\ell\ge N/3\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).
Donor unbiasedness, conditional independence, and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\mid z_0\}
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{m_\ell}
 \le\frac{3SdC_\Sigma}{N}.
\tag{16}
\]
Jensen's inequality, applicable because \(0<\lambda\le1\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^{2\lambda}\mid z_0\}
 \le(3SdC_\Sigma/N)^\lambda.
\tag{17}
\]
Combining (11)--(17), using \((x+y+z)^2\le3(x^2+y^2+z^2)\), gives
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\tau(z_0)\}^2
       \mid z_0,(X_{st})]
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 \le C R_{X,\mathrm{opt}},
\tag{18}
\]
where the last inequality is the rate equivalence in
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  This proves the
upper comparison without using the attainable-direction restriction.

We next prove the converse under the stated class-richness inequality.
For the treated-mean channel, fix admissible regression, design, and donor
laws with slack in the attainable-direction condition.  Let
\(b\in(0,B]\) be fixed and, under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), make the event outcomes
independent with values in \(\{-b,b\}\) and
\[
 \Pr_v(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b)=\tfrac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\tag{19}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma>0\), all probabilities lie in
\([1/4,3/4]\).  Consistency is imposed by setting
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\); the untreated potential means and the
training law are held fixed, so event-date transport and both conditional
centering equalities continue to hold.  The targets under \(v=1\) and
\(v=-1\) are separated by
\[
 \Delta_A=4b\sum_s\pi_s\varepsilon_s=4\gamma\sqrt A.
\tag{20}
\]
The Hellinger affinity of the observed event samples is
\[
 \prod_s(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-8\gamma^2/b^2),
\tag{21}
\]
where \(\log(1-x)\ge-2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) was used together with
\(\sum_sn_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  Taking \(\gamma\) small keeps
total variation bounded strictly below one.  The elementary nearest-target
test therefore gives minimax squared risk at least \(cA\).

For the fixed-design recovery channel, use the functions (5), scaled by a
fixed sufficiently small constant, and add to both candidate regression
vectors the same one-sided Holder cusp in a covariance-feasible direction
through \(z_0\).  The numerical condition on \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\) permits
the Holder and range radii to be divided so that the common cusp contributes
at least \(2c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\lambda\), whereas either signed
distance perturbation contributes at most
\(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\lambda\), for every
\(0<\delta\le\delta_0\).  Thus both laws satisfy
\texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}.  The perturbations vanish at every
realized \(X_{st}\), so the two conditional training laws can be chosen
identical.  Keep the donor and treated-observed laws identical and change
only the transported untreated potential mean as required by the two
regressions.  This preserves consistency, design-conditional centering,
and event-date transport, while (6) gives target separation at least
\(cD_X\).  The conditional observed laws coincide, so the nearest-target
test gives risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

Finally, \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies, under the
same displayed richness condition, two admissible laws with target
separation at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\) and total variation bounded away
from one.  It gives risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the largest of
the three subexperiment bounds and applying
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
 \ge cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.
\tag{22}
\]

It remains to retain, but correctly classify, the accepted anchor
certificate.  When \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\), the comparison pair
\((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) belongs to every anchor set
\(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\).  Thus \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) is impossible
conditional on this design, and optimality of the selected certificate gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le
 C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
The bandwidth floor implies
\((Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda\).
Because \(r=0\), every fitted intercept is a convex combination of the
replicated means.  Holder continuity, (23), and clipping therefore imply
\[
 |\mathbb E(\widehat m_{s\ell}\mid z_0,X,Z)-m_s(z_{0s})|
 \le C\{\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda
          +(h_s^\star)^\lambda\}.
\tag{24}
\]
The variance argument (12)--(13), now using the averaged local-constant
weights, remains valid.  Equations (16)--(17) and (24) give
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,X]
 \le CR_D.
\tag{25}
\]
The final inequality \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\) was proved in the
geometry lemma.  Nothing in (23)--(25) provides a lower bound by \(R_D\),
which is why the Gram radius is only an upper certificate.

Let \(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and
\(D_T=\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\).  On the regular anchor branch,
the anchor-certificate conclusion of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}
gives the conditional risk bound.  On the fallback branch,
clipping and bounded wealth bound squared error by \(16B^2\).  Averaging
over the exact design and applying
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{aligned}
\tag{34}
\]
Here fixed \(S\) and fixed positive cohort weights allow the second-moment
bound to pass through the weighted sum, and the fallback contribution
\(CT^{-2}\) is absorbed by \(D_T\).  This upper bound did not use
\texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus} or the numerical class-richness
condition.

For completeness, the replicated-smoothing expression is redundant.  Put
\(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Direct algebra gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{35}
\]
Consequently, because \(S\) is fixed,
\[
 \left\{\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{36}
\]

Under the displayed compatibility condition, the treated-sign experiment
in (19)--(21) gives a marginal lower bound \(cA\), and
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} gives \(cN^{-\lambda}\).
Fixing, for example, any error level in \((0,1/2)\),
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} gives two laws with
a common subprobability measure of fixed positive mass and target separation
at least \(cD_T^{1/2}\); the nearest-target test gives lower bound
\(cD_T\).  Taking the largest of these three subexperiments and using (36)
proves the reverse inequality in (34).

On the independent-calendar subclass, the no-log part of the anchor-moment
lemma proves the upper bound with \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the converse,
take a ball of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) about \(z_{01}\), and two Holder
regressions that agree outside that ball and differ at its center by
\(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  Add the same small attainable-direction component to
both surfaces; the class-richness inequality leaves enough Holder and range
radius for this addition.  The design probability of the ball is at most
\(C_Xv_dr_T^d\), and hence
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the ball for every }t\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0
\tag{37}
\]
for sufficiently small fixed \(c\).  On this event the two observed
regression experiments coincide, while their targets differ by
\(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Restriction to this common event and the
nearest-target test give the lower bound \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).
Substitution of \(S=1\), \(d=1\), and \(n_1=n\) yields the scalar display,
and (36) proves its claimed redundancy.

Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} identifies the causal target with
the observed-law functional.
We first establish coverage without using the class-richness condition.  On
the regular branch, condition on the exact design and donors.  The centered
unit-history contrasts obtained by replacing the nearest-site weights in
(12) with the actual selected local-polynomial weights have conditional mean
zero by \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; donor--panel separation
and cross-unit independence make them independent across \((s,i)\).  If an
uncentered contrast has support in \([a,b]\), convexity gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}
 \le\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}.
\tag{38}
\]
Applying (38) with the actual absolute weight sums and then exponential
Markov gives
\[
 \Pr\{\text{unitwise stochastic error}>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
       \mid z_0,X,Z\}\le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2.
\tag{39}
\]
The linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is the explicit bounded-range
correction; no variance is divided by.

For the calendar construction, apply the iterative beta-mixing replacement
argument from (28) to the two parity collections of complete cross-fitted
score blocks.  The score construction uses the actual response-independent
weights.  Conditional on the corresponding training folds, an independent
replacement block has range at most \(L_k\).  Applying (38) separately to
the two parities, adding the discarded-index bound \(L_{\mathcal G}\), and
using the bounded treated-mean radius \(r_B\) yields exactly
\[
 \Pr\{\text{calendar stochastic error}>r_{\mathrm{cal}}mid z_0\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}/2,
\tag{40}
\]
because the definition of \(x_{\mathrm{cal}}\) includes the replacement
budget \(2SK_T\beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\).  Since
\(r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\wedge r_{\mathrm{cal}}\), the event
that the stochastic error exceeds \(r_{\mathrm{samp}}\) is contained in the
union of the two events in (39)--(40), and therefore has probability at most
\(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}\).

For every balanced donor fold, spectral clipping gives
\(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I\).  Projection onto the cube is
nonexpansive, balanced splitting gives \(|I_\ell|\ge N/3\), and donor
unbiasedness and ellipticity give
\[
 \mathbb E\{\|\overline Z_\ell-z_0\|_2^2\mid z_0\}
 =\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)/|I_\ell|
 \le3SdC_\Sigma/N.
\]
Together with the deterministic spectral bound, this implies
\[
 \mathbb E\left[
 N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2
 \mid z_0\right]
 \le\frac{6SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{41}
\]
Markov's inequality and a union bound over at most two folds, with the
displayed value of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\), give
\[
 \Pr\left\{
 \max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 >q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mid z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{42}
\]
Projection is nonexpansive, while
\(\widehat\Sigma\preceq2C_\Sigma I\).  On the complement of (42), Holder
continuity, local-constant bias, and selected-certificate optimality bound
the conditional bias by \(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining
(39)--(42) and
\(\alpha=\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\) proves coverage at
least \(1-\alpha\) on the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch the
interval equals \([-2B,2B]\).  Bounded wealth and
\texttt{lem:causal-identification} imply
\(\tau(z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\), so coverage there is one.

We next bound length.  Since \(r=0\), every regular fitted response weight is
nonnegative and \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\).  Therefore
\[
 r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C_\alpha A^{1/2},
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{samp}}\le r_{\mathrm{unit}}.
\tag{43}
\]
The selected-certificate inequality follows directly by comparing its
minimizer with the admissible pair \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\).  Its bandwidth
floor makes
\((Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d)^{-1/2}\le(h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Donor
unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen give
\(\mathbb E\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\le CN^{-\lambda/2}\).
Combining these facts with
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&A^{1/2}
 +\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\\
 &+\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{aligned}
\tag{44}
\]
All small-sample branches in \texttt{def:honest-interval} are deterministically
absent eventually along the stipulated growth arrays.  The remaining
full-range contribution is bounded by
\[
 4B\Pr(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2},
\tag{45}
\]
which is absorbed by the spacing term in (44).  Equations (36) and
(43)--(45) prove the expected-length upper bound.  The independent-calendar
version follows by using the no-log conclusion of the anchor-moment lemma.

For the converse, let two observed laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\)
possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).
If \(I_\alpha\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under each law,
then
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}
 \ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Thus
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge |\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{46}
\]
Choose \(\gamma\) in (19) sufficiently small that (21) makes the common
mass exceed \(2\alpha\); (46) gives \(c_\alpha A^{1/2}\).  In the
covariance-aligned donor-location construction of
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family}, choose its fixed standardized
displacement multiplier sufficiently small.  The one-observation squared
Hellinger distance is quadratic in that multiplier divided by \(N\), so the
product common mass can be made greater than \(2\alpha\); the attainable
Holder direction still separates the targets by
\(c_\alpha N^{-\lambda/2}\).  Equation (46) gives the donor lower bound.
Finally,
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies common mass
greater than \(2\alpha\) and separation
\(c_\alpha\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  The independent-calendar
construction (37), with its ball constant chosen so that the no-hit mass
exceeds \(2\alpha\), supplies the no-log counterpart.  Taking the largest
channel and using (36) proves the expected-length lower bound.

Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), the integer-order convention gives \(r=0\), so
the Gram matrix is scalar.  Continuity and positivity of the fixed kernel on
a smaller ball provide \(k_0>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that
\(K(v)\ge k_0\) whenever \(\|v\|_2\le\eta\).  For
\(b\le\delta_0/\eta\), interiority and the conditional design-density lower
bound give
\[
 p_b:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\mid z_0\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d,
\tag{26}
\]
where \(v_d\) is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball.  If \(M_b\) counts
these visits, then
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge\frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.
\tag{27}
\]

We derive the needed mixing bound.  Split the calendar into consecutive
blocks of length \(a_T\), and within each parity retain alternating blocks,
so successive retained blocks are separated by a gap of length \(a_T\).
Iterating the defining absolute-regularity inequality shows that replacing
the retained blocks of either parity successively by independent copies
changes the probability of any event by at most the sum of the intervening
beta coefficients.  Across both parities this error is at most
\[
 2\left\lceil\frac{T}{a_T}\right\rceil
   \beta_0\rho_0^{a_T}\le CT^{-2},
\tag{28}
\]
because the definition of \(a_T\) gives
\(\rho_0^{a_T}\le(T\vee2)^{-3}\).

For an independent retained-block count \(Y_j\in[0,a_T]\), convexity of
the exponential on this interval gives, for \(\theta=a_T^{-1}\),
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-\theta Y_j})
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)
 \le\exp\left\{-\frac{1-e^{-1}}{a_T}\mathbb E(Y_j)\right\}.
\tag{29}
\]
Apply exponential Markov to the sum in each parity.  The common marginal
density makes the total expected count proportional to \(Tp_b\); the at
most two incomplete end blocks change it only by \(2a_T\).  Combining the
two parities with (28)--(29) gives constants \(c_1,C_1>0\) such that,
whenever \(Tb^d\ge C_1a_T\),
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\mid z_0\}
 \le C_1\exp\{-c_1Tb^d/a_T\}+C_1T^{-2}.
\tag{30}
\]
For smaller \(Tb^d/a_T\), the right side may be enlarged to one.  The
prescribed compatibility of \(c_G\) with the population local-constant Gram
bound makes (27) at least \(c_G\) on the complement of (30).

Put
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}
 \vee N^{-1/2}\vee(a_T/T)^{1/d},
\tag{31}
\]
and let \(b_q\) be the first dyadic grid point not below \(2^qb_\circ\),
whenever that point does not exceed one.  The grid already enforces its first
two floors.  Equations (27)--(31) imply
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>Cb_q\mid z_0\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{qd})+CT^{-2}.
\tag{32}
\]
Summing the dyadic tail in (32), and using the trivial bound
\(h_s^\star\le1\), yields
\[
 \mathbb E[(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0]
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.
\tag{33}
\]
Since \(a_T\asymp\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), (33) is the
claimed bound.  The exponent-\(\lambda\) assertion follows from
Cauchy--Schwarz.  At a fixed positive top bandwidth, (30) fails with
probability at most \(CT^{-2}\); on its complement the anchor set is
nonempty for every fold and cohort.  A union bound over fixed \(S K_N\)
therefore gives \(\Pr(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}\).
Under calendar independence, (28) is unnecessary and one may put
\(a_T=1\) throughout, replacing the logarithmic spacing term by
\(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(0<\lambda\le1\), so \(\kappa=\lambda\).  For every fixed exact
design \(X=(X_{st})\), every interior \(z_0\), and every
\(c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\), there are
constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class parameters,
such that
\[
 c\{D_X(z_0)\vee N^{-\lambda/2}\}
 \le \Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)
 \le C\left\{A^{1/2}+D_X(z_0)+N^{-\lambda/2}\right\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \asymp A\vee D_X(z_0)^2\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Moreover,
\(\omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda\),
while \(\omega_{s,X}(1;z_{0s})\ge c\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda\).
If \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\), then
\(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)\le C R_D\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(\rho_s=\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})\), \(D_X=\sum_s\pi_s\rho_s^\lambda\),
and \(A=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\).  We first prove the upper bound.  Take any
admissible \((f,g,z)\) in the definition of
\(\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)\), set \(q_s=f_s-g_s\), and let \(t_s\) be a
nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  The testing-distance constraint gives
\[
 |q_s(X_{s t_s})|\le n_s^{-1/2}.
\tag{1}
\]
Because the difference of two members of
\(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) is Holder with constant at most \(2L\),
\[
 |q_s(z_{0s})|
 \le n_s^{-1/2}+2L\rho_s^\lambda.
\tag{2}
\]
The donor part of the same constraint and
\(\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}\) imply
\[
 \|z-z_0\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Holder continuity of \(g_s\), followed by (2)--(3), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|
 &\le\sum_s\pi_s|q_s(z_{0s})|
     +L\sum_s\pi_s\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda\\
 &\le C\left\{A^{1/2}+D_X+N^{-\lambda/2}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Here
\(\sum_s\pi_s n_s^{-1/2}\le
S^{1/2}(\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s)^{1/2}\), and \(S\) is fixed.  Taking the
supremum proves the upper bound for \(\Omega_X\), and (1)--(2) also prove
the stated upper bound for \(\omega_{s,X}\).

For the spacing lower bound, let
\(\mathcal X_s=\{X_{s1},\ldots,X_{sT}\}\) and
\[
 q_s(x)=a\,\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathcal X_s)^\lambda,
\tag{5}
\]
where \(a>0\) is a sufficiently small constant depending only on
\(B,L,d\).  The distance map is one-Lipschitz, and for
\(0<\lambda\le1\),
\(|u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda\) for \(u,v\ge0\).

\[

\[

\tag{7}

proposed.name: Cohort fixed-design point modulus
proposed.construction:
Write
\[
 \mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}
 =\{f\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L):\|f\|_\infty\le B\}.
\]
For a fixed exact design array \(X=(X_{st})\), a cohort \(s\), an
evaluation point \(x\in[0,1]^d\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define
\[
 \omega_{s,X}(\varepsilon;x)
 =\sup\left\{|f(x)-g(x)|:
 f,g\in\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B},\quad
 n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\{f(X_{st})-g(X_{st})\}^2\le\varepsilon^2
 \right\}.
\]
This is a fixed-design optimal-recovery modulus.  The factor \(n_s\)
records the replicated-response testing information; it is not a variance
assumption about the calendar sequence.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the required replicated-response optimal-recovery primitive at a fixed realized design.

proposed.name: Full-covariance conditional product modulus
proposed.construction:
For \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_S)\in\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}^{S}\) and
\(z=(z_1^\top,\ldots,z_S^\top)^\top\in([0,1]^d)^S\), put
\[
 \mathcal T(f,z)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s f_s(z_s).
\]
For a fixed exact design \(X=(X_{st})\), an interior reference path
\(z_0\), a full covariance \(\Sigma\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define the
directed local product-experiment modulus
\[
\begin{split}
 \Omega_X(\varepsilon;z_0,\Sigma)
 =\sup\bigg\{&|\mathcal T(f,z_0)-\mathcal T(g,z)|:
 f,g\in\mathcal F_{\lambda,L,B}^{S},\ z\in([0,1]^d)^S,\\
 &\sum_{s=1}^{S}n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}
       \{f_s(X_{st})-g_s(X_{st})\}^2
   +N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z-z_0)\|_2^2\le\varepsilon^2
 \bigg\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus the response and generated-center coordinates share one constant
testing-distance budget.  The second term uses the full stacked covariance,
including every cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort entry.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The conditional difficulty must allow regression surfaces and the donor center to vary under a single testing budget using the full covariance.

proposed.name: Conditional optimal-recovery rate
proposed.construction:
For each cohort let
\[
 \rho_{sX}(x)=\min_{1\le t\le T}\|X_{st}-x\|_2,
 \qquad
 D_X(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda,
 \qquad
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\]
The conditional optimal-recovery squared-risk scale is
\[
 R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 =A\vee\Omega_X(1;z_0,\Sigma)^2.
\]
The finite nearest-site distances give a computable characterization of this
scale for \(0<\lambda\le1\), as proved in
\texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition installs the corrected fixed-design minimax scale and its computable spacing side.

proposed.name: Rough-Holder nearest-design optimal-recovery estimator
proposed.construction:
For every donor fold \(\ell\) and cohort \(s\), let
\[
 t_{s\ell}
 =\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{1\le t\le T}
       \|X_{st}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2,
 \qquad
 \overline Q_{st}=n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}Q_{sti},
\]
where the minimum in the first display is the smallest calendar index among
ties.  Define
\[
 \widehat m_s^{\mathrm{opt}}
 =K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}\overline Q_{s,t_{s\ell}},
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
 n_s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 -\widehat m_s^{\mathrm{opt}}\right\}.
\]
This measurable estimator is total for every \(N,T,n_s\ge1\).  It is the
rough-Holder optimal-recovery witness; the smoother anchor/extrapolation
estimator \(\widehat\tau\) remains the marginal-rate witness.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This total, measurable estimator attains the conditional modulus in the rough-Holder regime without treating Gram coercivity as a lower bound.

project_justification.fill: The note derives the causal observed-law functional, defines cohort and joint product-experiment moduli, and proves for rough Holder surfaces a premise-free conditional-risk upper bound and, under the disclosed class-richness condition, a matching frontier equivalent to treated replication, weighted nearest-site spacing, and donor location.  It retains the anchor/extrapolation rule as a computable upper certificate and proves its corrected marginal and honest-length rates.  The common-design-shock construction is excluded by design-conditional centering and is not used as a negative frontier result.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event paths have density bounded above and away from zero.  Conditional analysis uses their optimal-recovery modulus and nearest-site distances; Gram coercivity certifies one estimator but is never a minimax converse.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per calendar window and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes.  Conditional on the full exact design and realized path, untreated responses are centered at \(m_s(X_{st})\), treated outcomes retain their path-conditional mean, and unit histories are independent across units; within-unit temporal and training/event dependence remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; design-conditional centering does not identify this causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary, and the random-design density is bounded below there.  Exact fixed-design recovery can nevertheless be much easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the realized path.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event path is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nearest-site and local-constant weights are nonnegative.  The \(\lambda>1\) extension asks when signed higher-order optimal-recovery weights have a uniformly controlled conditional stochastic norm under the existing assumptions.

prose_updates.related_work: Donoho (1994) supplies the classical Gaussian optimal-recovery link between a linear-functional modulus and near-minimax affine estimation; the present result instead proves a rough-Holder, bounded-response product-experiment comparison with a generated full-covariance query.  Stone (1982) and Fan (1993) give ordinary Holder and pointwise local-polynomial benchmarks but not replicated sites plus a generated center.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) treat generated coordinates attached to every training row, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study classical error in every training coordinate; neither experiment applies here.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) evaluate a sample-split local-polynomial estimator at an estimated minimizer, but strong convexity makes its location error second order.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware interval calculations, and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) motivate dependent block calibration.  These sources inform the architecture; the nearest-site characterization, donor-product combination, and three-channel panel frontier are derived in this note.
prose_updates.interpretation: Conditionally, two exact designs with the same Gram certificate can have different difficulty: a site exactly at the event path removes the spatial recovery component, while a nearby hole leaves a Holder-sized ambiguity.  Marginally, random occupancy converts that ambiguity to the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds the maximum of treated replication and spacing; otherwise the generated center is asymptotically oracle-negligible.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion is conditional on observing every historical path exactly.  The conditional modulus and constructive frontier are proved for \(0<\lambda\le1\), where nearest-site and local-constant response weights are nonnegative and have unit absolute mass.  For \(\lambda>1\), the open extension is to characterize whether higher-order optimal-recovery weights can be selected with conditional stochastic norm uniformly controlled under the existing centering, cross-unit independence, and geometric-mixing assumptions; no new covariance-stability assumption is imposed here.  The geometric-mixing spacing logarithm is retained, with a no-log iid corollary.  Exact phase-intersection constants remain open after centering removes the obsolete common-design-shock witness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction.  Design-conditional centering is a separate observed-law sampling condition required for the replicated-response and treated-mean channels; it excludes the former common-design-shock witness but does not determine exact minimax constants.  Upper risk, coverage, and expected-length bounds for \(0<\lambda\le1\) do not require the lower attainable-modulus constant.  The donor and spacing converses use the disclosed sufficient class-richness inequality \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\).  Growing dimension, smoothness adaptation, uniform-in-path bands, exact constants, and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the realized value of \(z_0\), and abbreviate
\[
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
The random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\)-measurable because \(E\in\mathcal X\).  Therefore the asserted shock representation and the defining property of conditional expectation give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely conditional on }z_0.
\tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking conditional expectation of the shock representation given \(z_0\) yields \(\mu_{si}=bp_E\).  Combining this identity with (1)--(2) and squaring gives
\[
 0
 =\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2p_E(1-p_E).
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(b\ne0\), equation (3) implies \(p_E\in\{0,1\}\).

For the former scalar construction, \(z_0\) is fixed and \(X_{11}\) is uniform on \([0,1]\), so
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (3).  Hence its shocked law cannot satisfy \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, it cannot belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The all-zero law may satisfy the condition, but the former obstruction requires both laws to lie in the class, so that pair is unavailable.  Notice that no causal transport premise was used: the exclusion follows solely from the observed-law sampling-centering condition.

Let
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(W\) is bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable, the tower property and (4) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)\mid z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
For \(E\in\mathcal X\), take \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) in (5).  If \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)>0\), division by \(p_E\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.
\tag{6}
\]
Taking \(W=\mathbf 1_{E^c}\) gives the same equality on \(E^c\) when \(p_E<1\).  The common-design-shock exclusion now follows from \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

We next prove that the centering equality does not fix the event-noise constant.  It is enough to exhibit one admissible choice of fixed class parameters.  Take
\[
 S=1,\quad \pi_1=1,\quad H=0,\quad p=d=1,\quad z_0=\frac12,\quad
 \lambda=\kappa=1,\quad B=L=1,\quad \delta_0=\frac14,\quad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=\frac18,
\]
and take \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\); choose any \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  Put
\[
 m(x)=\frac12+\frac14\left|x-\frac12\right|,\qquad
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],\qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m(X_{1t}).
\tag{7}
\]
Let \((\xi_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) be independent Rademacher variables and set
\[
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j.
\tag{8}
\]
The donor sample is independent of the training array and of all event variables introduced below.  For every event unit set \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\), and hence, by \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.
\tag{9}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), let \((\varepsilon_i)_{i=1}^{n_1}\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the design and donors, and set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In both laws impose consistency by setting \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold definition then gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12\quad\text{under }P^{(0)},\qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i\quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.
\tag{10}
\]
The returns in this construction belong to \((-1,\infty)\).

We verify every class restriction used in asserting membership.  First, (7), (9), and (10) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|\le\frac58,\qquad |B_{1i}(0)|\le\frac12,\qquad |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The function in (7) has supremum at most \(5/8\) and Lipschitz constant \(1/4\), hence belongs to \(\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), verifying \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Also \(z_0=1/2\) is at distance \(1/2\ge\delta_0\) from the boundary, and the design density is identically one, verifying \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density}.

Conditional on the entire design, the training coordinates in each unit history are deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\) the event coordinates are deterministic, and under \(P^{(1)}\) they are functions of the independent \(\varepsilon_i\).  Thus the unit histories are mutually independent across \(i\) conditional on the design, as required by \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The sequence in (7) is independent over \(t\), so its beta-mixing coefficients are zero, verifying \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  The paths \(X_{1t}\) are observed exactly, verifying \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

The training centering equality follows directly from (7):
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m(X_{1t}).
\tag{11}
\]
By (10), independence, and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\), under either law
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0],
\tag{12}
\]
so \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} holds without imposing independence between a unit's training and event outcomes as a class condition.

From (8), conditional on \(z_0\), the donors are independent and identically distributed, have mean \(z_0\), and are separated from the training and event samples.  Moreover,
\[
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)=1,\qquad
 \mathbb E[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0]=1=B^4.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} all hold, and the full scalar covariance is retained rather than discarded.

Event-date transport follows from (7) and (9):
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=\frac12=m(z_0).
\tag{14}
\]
Finally, for \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), feasibility is guaranteed by interiority and (13), and \texttt{def:local-modulus} gives
\[
 \omega_P(\delta;z_0)
 =\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|
 =\frac14\delta
 \ge c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa.
\tag{15}
\]
Hence \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus} holds.  Consistency was imposed in (10), so all listed conditions in \texttt{def:panel-model-class} have been verified and \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).

The design, replicated-response, and donor laws are identical by (7)--(8).  By \texttt{def:target}, (9)--(10), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\),
\[
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)=\tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 =\mathbb E[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0.
\tag{16}
\]
Nevertheless, (10) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=\frac1{16},
\tag{17}
\]
and consequently the conditional variance of the treated sample mean is respectively \(0\) and \(1/(16n_1)\).  Equations (5)--(6) prove the repaired orthogonality, while (7)--(17) show that this repair alone does not determine the event-noise constant.  Therefore eliminating the former common shock cannot by itself answer the separate exact-constant problem for the remaining product experiment.

added_lemmas.statement: Can one construct a total feasible estimator and confidence interval that attain the exact asymptotic minimax constants for conditional mean squared error and uniformly honest conditional expected length at every intersection of the treated-mean and fixed-design optimal-recovery channels in the repaired class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), while estimating the full donor covariance \(\Sigma\) and accommodating calendar dependence?  The proposed handle is the ordered modulus of the joint treated-outcome, replicated fixed-design regression, and covariance-standardized donor-location product experiment.
added_lemmas.justification: Rate comparison does not determine the joint least-favorable experiment or its exact constants at channel intersections.
added_lemmas.gap: The repaired fixed-design optimal-recovery frontier leaves simultaneous exact constants with generated donor locations and calendar dependence unresolved.
added_lemmas.consumer: An exact solution would calibrate sampling allocation and interval length at boundaries between replication and proxy-location difficulty.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Every law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) satisfies the conditional orthogonality
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)\right\}W\mid z_0\right]=0
\]
for every cohort \(s\), unit \(i\), and bounded \(\mathcal X\)-measurable random variable \(W\).  Hence every design event \(E\in\mathcal X\) with \(0<\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)<1\) has the same conditional treated mean on \(E\) and \(E^c\), and \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} removes the former common-design-shock obstruction.  This repair does not by itself determine an exact asymptotic minimax constant: there are admissible scalar fixed class parameters and, for every positive \(N,T,n_1\), two laws \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\) having the same joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) and the same target \(\tau(z_0)=0\), while
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(0)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{P^{(1)}}(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Thus removal of the invalid witness is a necessary model repair, not a determination of the sharp constants for the remaining centered product experiment.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current negative frontier claim is false after the sampling-centering repair.  The replacement proves the valid implication of that repair and gives an explicit centered two-law certificate showing why exact constants remain a separate problem.
